segments.ch12.s0600: Let the jury consider their verdict.
segments.ch12.s0610: He had said it for about the twentieth time that day.
segments.ch12.s0650: The idea of having the sentence first!
segments.ch12.s0700: Alice had grown to her full size by this time.
segments.ch12.s0720: You are nothing but a pack of cards!
segments.ch12.s0730: At this the whole pack rose up into the air.
segments.ch12.s0740: They came flying down upon her.
segments.ch12.s0750: She gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger.
segments.ch12.s0760: She tried to beat them off.
segments.ch12.s0770: And found herself lying on the bank, with her head in her sister's lap.
segments.ch12.s0780: Her sister was gently brushing some dead leaves from her face.
segments.ch12.s0800: Why, what a long sleep you have had!
segments.ch12.s0810: Oh, I have had such a curious dream!
segments.ch12.s0820: So Alice got up and ran off, thinking what a wonderful dream it had been.
segments.ch12.s0830: But her sister sat still just as she left her, watching the setting sun.
segments.ch12.s0840: She was thinking of little Alice and all her wonderful Adventures.
segments.ch12.s0850: Till she too began dreaming after a fashion.
segments.ch12.s0860: The whole place around her became alive with the strange creatures of the dream.
segments.ch12.s0870: The long grass rustled at her feet as the White Rabbit hurried by.
segments.ch12.s0880: The frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool.
segments.ch12.s0890: She could hear the rattle of the teacups at the March Hare's never-ending meal.
segments.ch12.s0900: And the shrill voice of the Queen ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution.
segments.ch12.s0910: Once more the pig-baby was sneezing on the Duchess's knee.
segments.ch12.s0920: Once more the shriek of the Gryphon, and the squeaking of the Lizard's slate-pencil.
segments.ch12.s0930: All mixed up with the distant sobs of the miserable Mock Turtle.
segments.ch12.s0940: So she sat on, with closed eyes, and half believed herself in Wonderland.
segments.ch12.s0950: But she knew she had but to open them again, and all would change to dull reality.
segments.ch12.s0960: The grass would be only rustling in the wind.
segments.ch12.s0970: The pool rippling to the waving of the reeds.
segments.ch12.s0980: The rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep-bells.
segments.ch12.s0990: And the Queen's shrill cries to the voice of the shepherd boy.
segments.ch12.s1000: The baby's sneeze and the Gryphon's shriek would change to the noise of the farm-yard.
segments.ch12.s1010: And the lowing of the cattle far off would take the place of the Mock Turtle's sobs.
segments.ch12.s1020: Lastly, she pictured how this same little sister of hers would one day be a grown woman.
segments.ch12.s1030: And how she would keep, through all her riper years, the loving heart of her childhood.
segments.ch12.s1040: And how she would gather about her other little children, with many a strange tale.
segments.ch12.s1050: Perhaps even with the dream of Wonderland of long ago.
segments.ch12.s1060: Remembering her own child-life, and the happy summer days.
